orchestration: LangChain ChatOllama; ChatOpenAI for the llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible endpoint
json_enforcement: LangChain structured output with a Pydantic schema, followed by deterministic fact overrides
confidence_formula: rf_confidence = abs(rf_attack_probability - 0.5) * 2; emitted with model_used by fusion_layer.fuse_with_metadata
technique_precedence: Use RAG top-3 consensus; abstain with null technique_id/tactic when fewer than two hits agree

runtime_verification.prompt_eval_speed: not recorded: the measuring call reused the cached prompt, so its prompt_eval figure is inflated

quality_issues: Entity omission, not fabrication, is the dominant failure: strict entity preservation is 28/100 because the model leaves out a required IP or port, while 68/100 outputs are free of any foreign or altered entity. Roughly 72 of the 100 strict failures are omissions.

Few-shot entity copying occurred in 30/100 alerts (172.16.33.9, LMS-WEB03, DNS-INT02, 100.64.7.18); one alert was a near-verbatim copy of example 1. A two-layer control was added afterwards, see `few_shot_leak_control`. The re-measurement is not complete, so treat 30/100 as the last measured value, not the current one.

PortScan remediation suggests a WAF block in 5/7 PortScan alerts. The earlier claim that this happens 'for SMB traffic' is NOT supported: none of the 7 PortScan alerts had dst_port 139 or 445. WAF advice on a non-web port with a non-web label occurs in 8/100.
SSH-Patator explanations never state that the RAG evidence was insufficient: 0/7, although all 7 abstained so the prompt did require it. Across all 47 abstaining alerts it is stated in only 11.

The model names a technique id in its prose that was never retrieved in 7/100 alerts. The 53/53 `technique_in_hits` rate is true by construction (the draft schema has no technique field) and is a regression guard, not a measurement of the model.
87 of 399 claims are Thai prose or generic advice with no checkable entity and remain undecidable mechanically. Whether they are true needs human raters.
remediation_limit: 1-5 unique items: JSON schema maxItems plus a dedupe-and-truncate validator on LlmDraft
few_shot_policy: Few-shot entities must not match tests/fixtures; enforced by tests/test_llm_layer.py
quality_issues_fixed: Remediation loop: both alerts returned 3 distinct items, and response time fell from 18.9s to about 6s.
Abstention: with technique_id null, the SSH-Patator explanation no longer names a technique.
Priority: now derived by rule; SSH-Patator at fused_score 0.55 is MEDIUM as the fixture expects.
In the priority-rule rerun, remediation no longer named EternalBlue and the SSH alert no longer suggested a WAF.

priority_rule.rule: fused_prediction != 1 -> LOW; fused_score >= 0.80 -> HIGH; otherwise MEDIUM
priority_rule.inputs: fused_score and fused_prediction only; rf confidence is not used because it measures RF certainty in either direction, not attack risk
priority_rule.status: provisional: chosen to match the five tests/fixtures expectations, not tuned on data or validated with analysts

m2_measurement.status: measured once on 100 alerts; re-measurement after the few-shot fix is in flight
m2_measurement.evidence: reports/llm_faithfulness_raw.jsonl (one line per alert; every rate below is recomputable from it by hand)
m2_measurement.sample: 100 alerts, seed 42, stratified over 14 CICIDS-2017 attack categories (capped at 7 each so DoS Hulk and DDoS cannot dominate) plus 10 BENIGN. Per-category rates rest on 2-7 alerts and are descriptive only, not natural-traffic rates.
m2_measurement.pipeline: real deployed path per alert: RF + IF-v2 + AE-v2 scores, then fuse_with_metadata, then RagRetriever.retrieve(top_k=3) queried with the RF predicted label, then the LLM. The true label is never shown to the model.
m2_measurement.throughput: 61.4 tok/s pooled (median 60.4, range 52.0-70.8); 6.04 s mean wall time per alert; 2,192 token mean prompt; about 606 s for the run
not_measured: Whether the 87 undecidable claims are true. Needs human raters.
Whether 'supported' claims are true as whole sentences. Only their entities and terms are grounded.
Semantic errors with no lexical trigger; remediation quality or safety.
Hostname preservation on real data: CICIDS-2017 has no hostnames, so affected_asset falls back to dst_ip and the hostname check is unit-tested only.
Run-to-run variance (one draw per alert), human-vs-rule agreement, live PA-5220 alerts.
m2_measurement.no_llm_judge: No LLM was used to grade another LLM's output. Every rate above is either an exact string check or an explicitly-labelled lexical approximation.
m2_measurement.thesis_criteria: Both H2 criteria fail by a wide margin: hallucination 0.346 against a <=0.10 target, strict entity preservation 0.28 against a 1.00 target. This is not a tuning gap.

few_shot_leak_control.problem: The prompt had instructed the model not to copy from EXAMPLES since before the measurement, and it copied anyway in 30/100 alerts. An instruction that has already failed is not a control.
few_shot_leak_control.layer_1: FEW_SHOTS now carry placeholders ({{SRC_IP}}, {{ASSET}}, {{DST_PORT}}, {{TECHNIQUE_ID}}, ...) instead of realistic values. Two earlier attempts only swapped one realistic set for another, so there was still something plausible to copy.
few_shot_leak_control.layer_2: llm_explain._assert_no_foreign_entities rejects any output containing an IPv4, hostname-shaped token, or Txxxx id that is absent from FACTS. One corrective retry, then ValueError. It fails loudly on purpose: an explanation naming the wrong host sends an analyst to the wrong machine, which is worse than no explanation.
few_shot_leak_control.detection_is_shape_based: find_foreign_entities matches token shape, not a blocklist of the current example values, so the check keeps working when the examples change.
